messages.text: Mom wants the framed Hopkins hooding photo off the upstairs shelf before Sunday. Dad says his old College Park diploma is behind it, because of course he knows the shelf order.
That sounds exactly like him. I can grab both when I come by after the museum.
Also she found a box of her old student-schedule binders and his agency rollout binders. Your niece thinks they are ancient tablets.
Tell her the binders explain at least half of how we became this organized.
The cardiology portal locked me out again. I am fine, just need the lab PDF before Friday.
Send the screenshot. I can reset the login at lunch, save the PDF, and make a one-page list of what to ask Dr. Larkin.
Your mother already has the dates in a folder. You two move fast.
Fast is easier than guessing. Also please put the BP readings in the same folder, even the boring ones.
Found an old 2017 printout in the basement box. Page 4 says, in your handwriting, "stop being the API-only person."
Keep that one, please. Page 7 should have the intake screen sketch and the handoff after someone contests a decision.
It does. Also red circles around blank address-history fields and the contractor signoff boxes.
That was the first time the database diagram felt too small for the actual problem.
Dad found the museum passes for Sunday. Are you still thinking 11:30 before lunch?
Yes. I put 11:30 for the passes and 1:15 at Black Market Bistro. I can drive from D.C. and meet you both there.
That works. I will tell Andrew to come after soccer if they are bringing the little one.
I’ll text him too and ask if they need a high chair on the reservation.
I found your old school folder while clearing the hall closet. Do you want the Suburban Hospital wrist band and the Bethesda-Chevy Chase program, or should I recycle them?
Keep the wrist band for now. The B-CC program can probably go unless there are photos.
There are two photos from the Maryland History Day table, plus the family tree worksheet where you wrote Bradford, Miller, Walsh, and Campbell.
Save that packet. It will make Andrew laugh at Sunday dinner.
If I grab rice bowls on the way back, can you clear the coffee table before puck drop?
Yes. Red blanket, laptop off, no work tabs by 7.
Good. Also the ticket rep still has us under Reyes, not the long hyphenated version, so I left it alone.
Fine by me. Same seats, same couch drill.
I moved my 9:00 call to the dining table tomorrow. You can have the office for the release review.
Thanks. My chest finally unclenched after I made the prep list. It is always the hour before exec review that does it.
Then no bonus prep tonight. Dinner, walk, Caps. Also maybe keep that benefits-page note you made instead of letting it vanish again.
I bookmarked two names and closed the laptop. No standing thing on the calendar, just trying not to keep white-knuckling every launch.
Can you talk after your Hill call? Release slipped again, Dad's portal is locked, and I still said yes to the panel prep.
Yes. Start with the list. You have three things due before Friday and two of them came from automatic yeses.
I know. I haven't texted Maya yet because I wanted your read before I spin it into twelve tabs.
We'll sort what is actually due tonight from what only feels due tonight.
Can you look at the portal before Sunday? It says Dad and I should schedule the spring update, but the pharmacy page has three different buttons.
Yes. Bring the login and the Aetna cards to dinner. I want to compare it with Dr. Shah's note and the Hopkins explainer before we pick a slot.
Thank you. The last claim page also has a line I don't understand.
Send me a screenshot with the member number covered. Usually the billing part is more annoying than the appointment itself.
I found the little Metro cards from those Saturday trips downtown. One still has a Natural History sticker on it.
Keep it. I can still picture Andrew racing me to the elephant and me dragging everyone toward the Calder room after.
You also insisted on practicing your recital piece before we left, even if it made us miss the first train.
Middle C before Smithsonian stairs. Very balanced childhood.
For Sunday, Aunt Linda asked if you still want the porch table or if indoors is better.
Indoors is easier for me if people keep stepping outside after dinner. I can bring the window cracked and sit by you.
That is fine. Do you need me to put anything in the medicine basket for your shoulder?
No, I have a travel tube of Advil in my bag. Also bringing the two tiny 2.5 pieces from the D.C. shop for the card table, only if everyone is settled.
Do you still have the picture of the blue tiles from your Portugal trip? I wanted to show your father.
It is in the square-picture app. I put it in the same saved folder as the pastry place and the museum courtyard.
Thank you. I tried that black app again for news about the Metro work and gave up after three angry threads.
Same. I only open it when someone sends me a specific link now.
Can I borrow ten minutes before standup? I talked it through at home last night, but I need your options brain.
Yep. What are the choices on the table?
Drop panel prep, move tennis, or ask Jamal to cover the release notes. Michael already flagged that I volunteered for all three.
Then pick the one with the cleanest handoff. Start with Jamal if the notes are documented.
Family dinner Sunday is 5:30. Do not bring a 14-step dessert unless you enjoy being roasted.
Noted. I already moved the release notes out of Saturday night, so I can do something normal like salad.
Normal salad is accepted. Also please don't review the Nationals ticket PDF five times like last year.
Three times max. And no glass tonight; I am doing treadmill plus early plug-in-the-phone routine.
Your mother said you were at the library late. Was that the group with the laptops?
Yes. I used the same broken-permit example from work, just cleaned up so the teens could debug it.
Good practical problem. Better than toy examples.
Exactly. One ninth grader spotted the bad date validation before I did.
Your mother says the school-board forum is streaming Tuesday. Are you still comparing the questionnaire answers?
Yes. I have a grid going: Metro funding, school nurses, rent relief backlog, and who actually has a workable timeline.
That last column sounds like you. Send the link if there is one place to check registration status.
Will do. I already checked mine and Michael's, but I'll forward the DCBOE page after lunch.
Were you downtown again for the procurement demo, or camped at home today?
Home today. I was mostly in React and a Java service, then cleaned up the handoff notes before the 3:30 review.
Sounds like a contract milestone. Keep the notes plain enough that the non-technical reviewers can follow them.
That's the goal. Monday is the office whiteboard session for the Azure diagram, so I want the written version solid first.
Before Sunday, could you show me again where the dental claim form downloads? Mine keeps hiding the attachments.
Yes. I just did our March paperwork, so it is fresh. I can bring my laptop after the museum.
Thank you. Don't let that conference check distract you from resting after your release week.
It is just the one panel payment, thankfully. Everything else this month is the usual paycheck rhythm.
Are we still doing dinner at 7:15, or did your Friday run long?
Still coming. I need ten more minutes to finish comments on Priya's design doc and send Elena the plain-English version.
We'll keep the soup warm. You sounded very measured when you called at lunch, even with all those moving pieces.
Measured is the goal. I am at 44.5 for the week, so I am closing the laptop after I hit send.
Coffee still on for 9? I saw your recap from Wednesday getting passed around.
Yes. I want your read on whether the second paragraph sounds too much like a pitch.
Bring it. Also, that product pricing thread in the PM group got lively overnight.
I saved three comments from it. Useful angle for the April panel questions.
I saw the 7:10 mat block before your 8:30. Do you want the office after that or should I camp at the dining table?
Office after 8:05 would help. I moved the Friday mat thing up because the 6 pm version kept getting swallowed by release calls.
Makes sense. I will take the dining table until then and start coffee when you are done.
Thanks. I already put it in the app so I won't quietly replace it with email.
I saw your note in the sheet. My Friday transfer can cover the 56 side again unless you changed the formula.
Formula is the same after the paystub check. I cleaned up the grocery and house-service rows and left February at $9,500.
Good. The Chase and AmEx pulls are both full-statement on the 18th, right?
Yes. Nothing to touch there; just the house transfer and escrow note.
Can you resend the address for tomorrow? Your mother put 'near Georgetown' but I want the parking garage, not the restaurant.
Use the garage by Wisconsin. We can walk from our place after you park; it is easier than circling Glover Park.
Good. Also bring the tax PDF if you want me to sanity-check the 26,000 line before you send it.
Thanks. Michael and I will mark the deductions first so it is clear what number the form wants.
For the museum tomorrow, do you want us to pick a cafe with indoor seating?
Indoor would be smart if the trees are still dusting everything. I already packed the tiny eye drops and a scarf.
Good. And don't carry that laptop bag on one side all afternoon.
I booked the 25-minute table work by Union Station after, then I'll do the short stretch video before dinner.
Your mother says Sunday dinner works at 5:30. Do I set two places for you and Michael?
The cardiology portal says I need to confirm the March 18 follow-up and upload the insurance PDF. Can you look at it after dinner?
Yes, two. We're coming straight from the condo after dropping the donation bags downstairs.
Yes. Bring the laptop Sunday. Also please don't shrug off the new copay note if it shows up before then.
Good. Bring the small box from your hallway if you still want it out of sight.
It's only showing $400 as the estimate, probably less after they process it.
I think it can finally go. Michael and I talked it through again this week.
Okay. If we need to float it while the portal sorts itself out, checking can handle that without touching investments.
Your mother said you are going to that library meeting Wednesday. Is this another one where they ask residents for three-minute comments?
Yes. I am trimming mine to concrete fixes: independent review seats, faster public files, and sending trained outreach teams when the call is really about someone needing help.
Keep the example short. The porch package file and those two Connecticut Ave pull-overs are enough personal context.
Exactly. I am not trying to make it about me, just enough to explain why the process side matters.
Could you bring the larger-print form Sunday? The portal keeps making me pinch the screen, and my fingers are not cooperating this week.
Yes. I'll print it and bring the adaptive pen too. Do you want yellow tulips again for the small vase?
Yellow, please. She always noticed those first. Your father says his morning number was fine, but make him show you the actual list.
I'll ask before dinner, casually. Also bringing the lemon cookies so we don't have to make them from scratch.
Caps tickets for Saturday are $86 each. Still want me to hold two?
Skip them. Put that toward the Portugal folder if the May street-music dates still work.
Got it. And keep Istanbul parked until taxes clear?
Yes. I want it on the list, but not at the expense of the IRA bump.
Your mother said you were comparing evening programs. Make sure the time commitment has a real payoff.
That's the question. The short exam path is clear; the longer school option only makes sense if it helps me run bigger cross-functional rooms.
Then ask what authority it gives you that your work record doesn't already show.
Exactly. I wrote that in the margin next to the city benefits rollout example.
For the museum volunteer form, do you still want me to list Maryland first and the business program second?
Yes, that order is right. The Maryland one was the CS track.
There is also a line asking whether you have a current campus schedule or any service record number. I can leave both empty?
Leave them empty. Nothing active there, and I have never had a number for that.
Are you still doing the long table this Saturday? I saw nice spring onions at the Bethesda market.
Yes. I may grab those if I end up doing the leek tart instead of the mushroom one.
Your father says not to overdo it. Also, I have the big white platter if you need it.
Platter would help. I have the bottles sorted, just need the market vegetables and one Trader Joe's stop.
Are you still leaving by 5:40 for Capital TC?
Yes. Court 3 at 6:30, and I already muted the release thread until after dinner.
Good. Pack the black brace this time; you forgot it last Tuesday.
In the bag with the band exercises. I am not repeating last year's nonsense.
Your mother found the brass candle snuffer from St. Luke's in the basement box. Do you want it, or should we donate it with the hymnals?
Donate the hymnals. Keep the snuffer until I can look through that box after my Saturday woods loop.
Fine. Basement table, left side. We are leaving for the 5 pm program, so come before dinner if you want quiet.
Perfect. I will be much easier to be around after the trees and mud.
Coffee Friday still works? I can do 8:45 or 9:00 near Farragut.
9:00 is better. I have the mat block at 7:15 and want ten minutes to enter it before I switch modes.
Good. What are the options if the prep deck tries to eat that slot again?
Option A is leave it untouched. Option B is move coffee, not the block. I am choosing A unless something is actually on fire.
You really made a spreadsheet for a primary with like four contested lines?
Five, if you count the delegate slot. Also the voter guide buried the paid-leave question on page 7.
Of course you found page 7. Any names you are knocking off because their climate plan is just clip art?
A couple. I care less about the slogan and more about whether they can get electrification money through agencies without a three-year procurement swamp.
Your mother says you offered to redo the portal instructions for us. We only need the appointment button and the password steps.
I can make a one-page version after my 7:00 walk, not the full annotated guide I started.
Parking at the museum opens at 10. Do you need to move us later?
No, 10 works. I am handling the 8:00 planning call, then reviewing Nate's branch before I leave.
One page is sufficient. You have the quarterly review today, correct?
Yes. I checked the deck before breakfast and put a hard stop on edits at 4:30.
You always seem to have the checklist before everyone else has the question.
That helps when the release board is red before coffee. Elena asked me to keep the payment folks moving until she is out of budget review.
Your mother found another envelope from the old campus servicer. Do you still need those records?
No, that account has shown $0 for years. Shred it unless it has tax language.
Understood. Also, when you come Sunday, can you look at our portal login?
Yes. I am bringing the March sheet anyway; Michael and I are aiming for the normal $8,500-ish month after February.
Your mother says you have the table handled for the 22nd. What time did you put us down for?
6:30 at Clyde's in Chevy Chase. You two, me and Michael, Andrew's crew, plus Michael's parents if they can get across from Falls Church by then.
Good. Send me the address and I will stop asking.
Sending now, with the parking note. I also marked who is driving versus Metro in the shared doc.
For Sunday, your mother says the Kreeger has an 11:30 entry. Parking looks limited.
I can meet you there. I'll come from the canal side if the morning is dry, then grab the Red Line plus a short ride.
Efficient. Send us the exact corner when you know it.
Will do. If we finish early, there's that Italian place near Dupont I wanted you both to try.
Before your presentation, eat something real. Your father used to go into those briefings on coffee and make himself shaky.
I had toast. Mostly I am over-rehearsing and checking Slack every 30 seconds.
You can ask someone neutral about the over-yes problem without turning it into a weekly project.
That is the appeal. One practical hour about stopping at reasonable, not another permanent obligation.
When you scan the Hopkins photo, please include the little program booklet too. The one with my practicum supervisor's note tucked inside.
I saw it beside Dad's College Park folder and the thick binder with all the milestone charts.
Yes, he saved every chart from those agency projects. I only saved the student letters that still make me smile.
I will scan both piles separately so nothing gets mixed.
For Sunday, I made a folder: museum passes, Dad's parking printout, and the insurance letter. Too much?
Not too much. I'll bring the laptop and we can do the letter after lunch, before Andrew and Emma arrive.
I was going to say I feel scattered, but the folder helped.
Same family reflex. Museum first, paperwork second, dessert as a reward.
Shared office is yours for the 10:00 exec review. I can take the dining table until noon.
Thanks. After that I need 20 minutes to upload the four-year service badge thing and the learning-fund receipt.
Good. Also block the sick hours for Friday if your voice is still rough. You earned using the banked time.
I will. The civic-tech panel prep can wait until Saturday; no extra calls tonight.
I almost wrote a whole thing where everyone could see it, then closed the app.
Good call. Send the useful parts to Maya or the tiny thread instead.
I sent Maya the rough version. She already asked for options, naturally.
That sounds like her. Coffee tomorrow should help you sort the rest.
Can we park the stroller in your second room Sunday, or is Michael using it for calls again?
Second room is free after 2. His climate brief is earlier, and my deck review is at the dining table.
Look at you two, scheduling the apartment like a tiny federal agency.
Condo bylaws require order and snacks. Bring the kid; we have museum passes printed.
Nats tickets for Sunday are still cheap. You in, or are you protecting your fancy sinuses from the upper deck?
Upper deck is fine if I can bring sunglasses and the little pharmacy pack. I also need an aisle seat so I can roll out my upper back like an elderly turtle.
I'll get aisle. Please do not bring a foam roller to section 313.
Are you free Sunday or are you doing another badge-and-lanyard thing?
Deal. I have a 7-minute app thing for the Metro ride and a real appointment Tuesday if the desk knot keeps being annoying.
Sunday dinner works. The lanyard thing is Tuesday, and I only have eight minutes on the agenda.
Eight minutes still means you will make a 30-slide backup deck.
Twelve slides. Plus a few notes from the cloud-sec channel because someone asked about defaults.
Can you send me the place you saved near the Air and Space museum? We may take Ellie Sunday.
Yes, I have it bookmarked with the dumpling place and that Madrid alley album. I will DM it from the photo app.
Do not send me another 40-post policy fight from the black app. I still have scars from the last one.
You are safe. I barely scroll there anymore. Too many loud posts before one useful thing.
Still good for 8:15? I can grab the corner table if you want less noise.
Yes please. I have the release mess down to three bullets from last night's texts.
Bring them. We'll do options first, then pastries.
Perfect. Keeping it between you, Michael, and the small thread was the right move.
For coffee today: do you want options on the PMI packet, the Hopkins evening info session, or the org-chart conversation?
All three, unfortunately. I need the path that gets me closer to shaping the work, not just cleaning up after roadmap decisions.
Coffee at 9:15 still okay, or did the condo-key errand eat your morning?
Then bring the notes from the 311 intake redesign. That's your cleanest example.
Still okay. The front desk only needed both fobs reactivated after the lobby update.
Good call. It shows the team mechanics and the resident outcome without sounding like a speech.
Nice. Also, did you decide on the extra room, built-ins or keep it flexible?
Built-ins. We keep circling back and the practical version wins.
Coffee still good at 9:30? You sounded like you needed a real offline block after this sprint.
Yes. Tuesday helped, even though I lost the second set 6-4.
Options: brag about the first set, ice the wrist, or pretend the scoreboard was a usability test.
First set bragging, then ice. No typing until I finish this coffee.
For tomorrow, am I bringing bread or the spreadsheet people are covering carbs?
Bring bread if you pass a good bakery. Jamal is bringing a cheese board and Priya claimed dessert.
Options question: red first with the main, or are you making us compare the two whites again?
Red with the braise, one white while people arrive. I am testing whether the Sauvignon Blanc fights the herbs.
I started the pasta water. Want the usual cooking soundtrack or Caps pregame?
Put on the Beethoven second movement. I need ten minutes of order before tomato sauce chaos.
Done. Also your left hand was tapping the counter like scales again.
Old habit. If I start counting aloud, please stage an intervention with parmesan.
Capitals game is getting tense. Want tea, Advil, or the heating pad before overtime?
Heating pad and maybe one Advil. Nothing stronger; I need my head clear for the morning prep.
Got it. Also I moved the little tin from the pantry to the top shelf so the niece visit tomorrow stays uncomplicated.
Thanks. Those are really just for adult dinners a few times a year, not normal weeknights.
Can you send that beginner Python link for Sophie? She keeps asking how the turtle square worked.
Sure. I used it with the library crew last week after the girls at table two asked for something visual.
Nice. Also very you to turn a Saturday into public utility plus homework rescue.
It was only 90 minutes. Easier than untangling the agency backlog.
Mom says you took the good box. Did it have my Whitman soccer photo or just your Bethesda greatest hits?
Mostly my stuff: camp forms, B-CC debate, and a tiny envelope from Sibley with my name spelled in Mom's handwriting.
Classic. Dad also wants the family sheet back; he said the Walsh/Campbell branch has the Civil War pension clipping tucked behind it.
I scanned it. I'll bring the originals when we come to Silver Spring.
Mom wants to know if you and Reyes are coming after the Caps matinee or before.
After. We already blocked the living room from 1 to 3:30.
Classic. Bring the 2016 photo if you still have it on the fridge; she wants to scan it.
It is still there, somehow. We will bring it with the dessert.
Dad sent me a photo of the cuff screen instead of typing the number. Classic.
Forward it? I want to compare it with the March 1 reading before I nudge him about the follow-up.
Sent. Also, are we still doing the blue tin thing on the 20th, or did Mom move it to Sunday dinner?
Sunday. Easier to combine with forms, the pharmacy stop, and Michael's check-in with his mom.
Found the old poster tube in Dad's basement while looking for the museum passes. Yours has a Sharpie date from June 2020 on it.
Keep it for now? I may want the sign-in QR sheet photo that was tucked inside. It has the names of two local groups I sent money to afterward.
Sure. Also Mom asked whether your porch-camera screenshot ever turned into anything or just a file number.
Just a file number and a follow-up email. Useful example, though, when people assume every call needs the same kind of response.
Your mother says I have to ask you before I choose the grocery-store clinic. The site says no charge, then another screen says pending review.
Your mother says the Skyline Drive cabins released October weekends. Do you still want me to check parking at Big Meadows?
Choose the one Dr. Shah's office listed. The no-charge screen is probably right, but I want the confirmation number before you go.
Yes, please. If the leaf weekend is under $240 all-in, I can fit it after the March transfer.
Efficient as always. I printed the confirmation page.
I will look after lunch. No sense overpaying when the same trail is there two weeks later.
Good. Also ignore the forwarded Facebook chart. I found the same question answered in the NIH Q&A and it matches the office note.
Aunt Denise's county form kicked her back to the first page when she left the father's middle name blank. Does she really have to mail the challenge packet?
Have her send screenshots before she starts over. I want to see which fields block submit and whether the phone route gives a tracking number.
This is why you get impatient with forms that assume everyone has the same paper trail.
Especially when that paper trail affects housing placement, school paperwork, clinic referrals, and who gets believed during a review.
Washer repair guy just left. Estimate is $397 if we replace the pump, or he can limp it along for a few weeks.
Do the pump. The operating account has enough after mortgage draft and groceries clear.
Got it. I won't move anything from Vanguard.
Thanks. I already adjusted the March sheet so the must-pay multiple stays above 5.8 after the repair.
I found the box with your College Park programming-team shirt and the case-competition binder. Want them brought Sunday?
Bring the binder, please. The shirt can stay in the basement unless Andrew wants to tease me.
Also, the benefits packet I scanned asks for current student ID and veteran preference documents. I assume neither applies.
Correct. I only need the old transcript dates and the later program dates.
Coffee this Friday still works? Or are you doing the family St. Alban's thing again?
Coffee still works. The St. Alban's thing is Mom's lane; I only promised to help set up chairs once.
Got it. Do you want post-coffee walk-and-talk or sit inside like normal people?
Walk-and-talk if it is not pouring. I have been staring at release notes too long and need actual air.
Can you still grab her from the museum Saturday, or did another courthouse thing eat your weekend?
Saturday is still fine. This week is only Wed office and Thu client room, then Friday at my kitchen table fixing Python data checks.
Only you would make 'kitchen table' sound like a command center.
It has coffee and fewer badge readers. I just need the SQL results to match before I send the packet.
Can you pause the Caps replay for five? I just added the family spreadsheet to tomorrow and now the deck is half-done.
Pausing. This is the same chain: urgent email, quick yes, then your real work moves to 10 pm.
That's annoyingly accurate. I'll ask Maya in the morning which one to hand back without making it weird.
Good. Tonight just write the two slides that unlock the rest.
Can you send the Sunday plan again? I know, I know, read the doc.
10:45 pickup from Silver Spring if your car seat is already in. Lunch is 12:15. Mom and Dad are coming straight from Maryland.
Car seat is in. Kid has strong opinions about the dinosaur room.
Perfect. I’ll move the museum slot earlier and keep the dinner headcount at seven unless Michael’s parents decide to join after NoVA traffic calms down.
Following up from last night's home audit: I need to give one thing back before noon.
What are the options?
Family spreadsheet, extra review for Priya, or tennis signup. Michael's vote was the extra review because I offered before anyone asked.
Agree. Send Priya one clean sentence and keep the rest of the morning intact.
Mom says you made a shared checklist for Sunday. Are we assigning pie slices now?
Only if you want the nine-year-old managing us. I added museum tickets, Dad's portal reset, and your school-form question.
That is annoying and useful. Emma wants to show you her Scratch project before dinner.
Perfect. I'll review bugs with her, then we can all argue about the Nats like normal people.
If you are still digitizing, label my boxes by agency and fiscal year. The rollout plans make no sense if the dates are out of order.
Already doing that. Mom's boxes are by student year and workshop type.
Good. Her placement notes are more useful than my status decks, frankly.
Disagree, but I will preserve both filing systems.
Coffee still on? Bring the 2017 before-and-after story if you want a quick pass before your talk.
Yes. I can show the path from batch jobs and database tickets to owning intake screens, hosting choices, release tradeoffs, and the questions from the program office.
Use one concrete path: login, document upload, notice, what happens when the data is absent.
Good. Then one slide with the same pattern showing up in leases, school forms, clinic referrals, and investor intros.
Coffee debrief: did the Shaw session work, or did the intake-form example go too bureaucratic?
It worked once I let them rename the variables. Three girls made the eligibility checker less awful than our real one.
That is both funny and a little damning.
I know. March total is 3 hours, which is about right before release week eats my evenings.
Coffee moved to 2:30. What are the options before Monday's panel?
Option A: rehearse once and stop. Option B: keep rewriting until midnight and show up wired.
Choose A. Also did you ever use the list from your benefits search, or is it still a browser tab museum?
Still a tab museum. I keep thinking a single outside voice would help me stop volunteering for every hard thing, then I punt.
Lena wants to know if Aunt Brittany's Saturday plan includes the giant gems or the rocket hall.
Gems first, rockets if she survives my two-minute story about Dad losing us near the Hope Diamond case.
Please spare her the full Bradford field trip archive.
No promises. I might also show her the keyboard upstairs at home if she asks how recitals worked before tablets.
For the renewal form, your mother found the earliest address as the apartment off Connecticut Ave, then the Bethesda house after that.
That matches what I remember them asking for. I only need the dates before the first River Road place.
The travel page is easy: London 2007, Montreal 2011, Florence 2019. No old lease or school paperwork from anywhere else in the folder.
Perfect. I'll enter it this afternoon before the site times out again.
Museum cafe has outdoor seating today. Your uncle may step out after lunch like usual.
I'll take the indoor table with Mom when he does. Easier on my clothes and my throat.
Do you want me to pick up anything from the pharmacy before we leave Maryland?
Just the store-brand acetaminophen if they have the small bottle. The 2.5 mints can stay home; wrong setting.
Coffee after tennis or before? Also send me the reel with the new mezze place when you find it.
After. I saved the reel next to the Hirshhorn exhibit post and Sara's doubles photos.
Options: 11:30 at Compass or noon at Slipstream. And I am not checking the black feed for the transit thread unless it is essential.
Noon works. I will send you the one clean link if it survives the pile-on.
Do you still have that link you used for Mom? Jess's group chat is arguing about whether to wait until after spring break.
I'll send the peer-reviewed roundup and the Post health desk piece. I would still check with your pediatrician for Lily's timing.
Thanks. Also did CareFirst ever fix your claim thing?
After 31 minutes on hold, yes. The visit stayed covered; they just coded the lab line weirdly.
Can you and Michael come by before the museum? Your father found the little guest book from the 2016 dinner.
We can stop in at 11. He wants to be back by first pitch.
Of course he does. I will make coffee early and send you both home with the envelopes.
Sunday dinner is 5:30. Mom says bring whatever survives your color-coded calendar.
Tell her the calendar is behaving. This week has tennis Tuesday, the Friday 7:15 mat slot, Saturday walk, and your museum niece time if you still want coverage.
Coverage accepted. Also, you are absolutely counting chasing a seven-year-old through Air and Space as a green square.
Only if the app lets me add stairs. I still need one real check after that.
Mom says you skipped the family thread tonight. Court night?
Just got home from Capital. Won the tiebreak and left the phone in the locker, which was the best part.
Look at you, disciplined. Wrist behaving?
Mostly. Brace for the last set, and I am dictating replies tonight.
I found the old binder from my night classes. Tabs everywhere. Do you want it for your study pile?
Yes, please. My dining table is already half practice questions and half notes for that bigger-room conversation.
Bring it Sunday. I still think your strongest examples are the ones where someone outside the office actually felt the difference.
That's the theme I'm trying to keep. Useful systems, calmer teams, fewer people stuck in a broken process.
